page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The configuration is built around the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture, delivering 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by 64.0 GB of memory to yield an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Networking provides a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the server includes 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage with no hardware GPUs attached.

Benchmark evaluations reveal standout memory throughput, with PassMark memory testing placing the instance in the top 10% of evaluated hardware. Measured memory read speeds reach 774.56 GB/s for cached blocks and 181.03 GB/s for large uncached transfers, accompanied by a Redis throughput of 12.13 million operations per second. General compute results on stress-ng and Geekbench fall within the average range, including a multi-core score of 8,241. Tradeoffs emerge in raw CPU-bound mathematical operations and cryptographic tests, where PassMark scores rank in the lower quartile, alongside slow token generation during LLM inference.

The dense memory configuration paired with local high-speed NVMe storage offers strong operational efficiency for I/O-sensitive, memory-bound workloads. Typical suitable deployments include Redis and Memcached clusters, relational and key-value database engines, data pipeline ETL tasks, and high-concurrency static web serving requiring fast ephemeral scratch space.

Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance supplies 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation, alongside 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier memory subsystem throughput, with PassMark memory scoring in the top 10% and cached memory read rates reaching 774.56 GB/s, while general compute scores reflect mid-range performance. Cryptographic and certain single-threaded LLM operations show comparative weaknesses. The high memory density combined with fast local NVMe storage provides strong resource efficiency for memory-heavy workloads, including Redis caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, data transformation pipelines, and high-throughput static web serving.
